title: Blood thinner dose mistake

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Hi, my name's Adam, I'm a junior doctor. Could I check your full name and date of birth?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, Harry Miles, 21st of the 10th, 1998.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Great. And how's your knee, Harry?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yeah, yeah, it's all right. So I mean, I'm sure you're aware, but I snapped my ACL when

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I was playing a bit of football. And then I had some surgery on it to get it sort of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: reattached. Surgery went fine, but then a couple of days later it got quite swollen,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: it was really painful. Someone said that my blood levels were quite low, so I had to have

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: a blood transfusion after that. Sort of connecting dots and that, I'm assuming I had a bleed

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: on my knee. But now it seems all fine now. I'm working with a physio, so hopefully I'll

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: be back playing as soon as I can.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Great. And do you understand why you had the bleed or has anyone spoken to you about

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: why you had the bleed?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No one specifically told me about why I was bleeding. I just assumed that with how I broke

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: it, maybe the stress meant I wasn't healing as good as I could have, or I don't know,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I don't know really, just sort of one of those things.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Okay. Has anyone spoken to you about your medications?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I know I was on a blood thinner for a little bit because I wasn't going to do as much sort

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: of moving around as I normally would, and I think that put me at risk of blood clots

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: and things like that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Are you worried that you had a bleed?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I wasn't, but the way that you're sort of asking these questions, is there like a, have

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I got a diagnosis or is there like another reason?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Just to reassure you, there isn't another diagnosis, you are recovering, but I'm going

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: to explain a bit more about why we think you had the bleed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: The reason I've been asking about all your medications is because one of the drugs you

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: have prescribed, the anticoagulant, which is a blood thinner, was mistakenly prescribed

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: at a higher dose than you needed, and that might have caused or contributed to your bleed.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I'm really sorry this happened.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: How does that happen? This shouldn't happen. It can't happen. If that had been another

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: drug, I literally could have died.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So I 100% agree with you, this shouldn't ever happen. Do you want me to explain what might

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: have happened?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Yes, please.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So this drug should have been prescribed as a lower dose for you to prevent blood clots

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: from happening because you're less mobile after your surgery. We also use the drug to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: treat blood clots, which needs a higher dose, and you were mistakenly prescribed the higher

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: dose.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I know it's a lot to take in. We sincerely apologise that one of the members of the team

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: prescribed the anticoagulant.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Hang on a minute, don't go and try to lay the blame onto somebody else. You're all part

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: of a team, okay? Somebody's got to be double checking doses, surely, of all things. So

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: don't come here acting like a messenger, okay? You're the whole team, okay? You're all taking

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: responsibility for that.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I 100% agree with you. It is all of our responsibilities to get this right. Do you have any more questions

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: at this point?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: What happens now? What happens from here?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: So you'll continue your rehab. I've personally double checked your medications to make sure

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: all of your prescriptions are correct.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Thanks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: We've discussed this as a team because we want to prevent this happening again, and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I've submitted a formal incident report as well, again for the same reason, so we can

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: prevent this happening to anybody else.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Well I'd like to put in a formal complaint as well for your department because this can't

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: happen, and I think the more attention it gets, the less likely it will.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I understand. I'll get you a form so you can make a formal complaint to the liaison service.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Do you have any other questions?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: No, I need some time to process this.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: I understand. If you think of any more questions then write them down and I'll come back and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: speak to you later today.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.text: Thank you.

notes: Complex discussion about error, responsibility and follow-up; no exact drug/dose supplied
